# Read selected per-effect resident observations through both SDKs

Parent: #763. Astra xhigh scope, 2026-09-13. Inspected frozen #775 delivery `d6509e4c72680acc7b93a0887b1f719c3cf449ce` in `/tmp/miso-engine-775`; its accepted product source is `559c23a36e6827f715798aa82d9aa498e3205d4f`. Delivery baseline is merged main `fbfce55b4c0441128ea513162bfe016c6a624935` (PR #776; required qualification `34738424659` PASS; #775 CLOSED). Preserve #775's working EQ/input-filter preview and paused #774 history. No old catalog/projection brief is a dependency.

## Requirements first and choice

The original parent requires per-effect observations retaining their original L/R values, spans and sequences, browser/headless parity, selective reads and honest timing while preserving legacy GR aggregates. It also requires full live response/composition, generic subscription sharing/lifecycle, spectrum, common clocks/envelopes, remote vectors and joins; this child does not claim those complete.

**Approve this one half-day product slice: read selected already armed resident taps through the SDK.** A caller can distinguish the compressor and limiter on one track and correlate their actual observation windows, instead of receiving only the track's folded GR number. Existing observe commands continue to arm/disarm and select window length. This is a usable observation consumer, not a new service framework.

Why this next: `EffectObservationHandle` already owns stable track/slot IDs, rack/index, the effect descriptor and one `ObservationReader` per tap. `ObservationWindow` already contains exact L/R, `[first_sample,end_sample)`, blocks and u64 sequence. `ReadyOwnership` already has these handles, command addressing and admitted armed masks; SDK console and shipped host already send observe commands. In contrast, live current-graph EQ composition needs new scalar/bank/builtin snapshot publication plus unfloored composition and real state binding. Do that when its usable path is ready, not as another prerequisite to exposing existing data. Do not add an explicit-chain preview utility that duplicates that future graph path.

## Product/API contract

Add an additive `readObservations(selections)` method to `OfflineEngine` and the browser engine/shipped host (headless synchronous, browser Promise, matching existing host conventions). Each selection explicitly names a **stable** `(trackId, rack, effectSlotId, tapId)` and requested channel(s). A single bounded call reads one latest complete window per selected tap. No implicit all-track read, background timer, callback stream, Worker, new subscription API, sharing cache or retained cursor.

Example workflow: prepare the existing console/observation capacity, arm two taps with the existing `console.submit(...observe(...))` or `host.observe(...)`, render, then read the two explicit stable tuples. Return the admitted command acknowledgement separately; it is not proof that a new window already exists. Documentation shows this through both SDKs.

Return results in caller selection order, containing actual resolved stable tuple, native effect ID, tap identity/descriptor, sample rate, selected independent values in the **owner's declared native unit**, and the untouched window's `firstSample`, `endSample`, `sequence` and `blocks`. JavaScript u64 fields are bigint. No lane max, cross-effect aggregate, inferred span or fabricated timestamp. The descriptor's unit/display-unit distinction remains visible: e.g. a linear reduction word is not mislabeled dB. This slice performs no new logarithm/unit conversion in a Worklet message handler and no client DSP. Existing generated observation metadata already declares units/folding/ranges; reuse it.

Distinguish a missing/unsupported target or unprepared observation capacity (typed refusal) from a known tap with no published complete window (`pending`) and an unarmed tap (`unarmed`). A valid published zero is a ready zero-valued observation. Returned primitive values/objects are owned and remain stable after later reads/renders/reload/dispose. Latest means latest publication, not a history or synchronized bundle: selected taps may have different original spans and sequences.

Do not relabel a retained pre-rearm window as a new publication from that arm. Use the existing admitted boundary/publication information to suppress it until a fresh window, or explicitly identify it as historical; no render-side epoch framework is required. Likewise do not attach a newly requested window length to an old window; return its actual `blocks`/span.

Resolve stable IDs against the current host's immutable compiled session/actual prepared handles. A caller-provided effect type or array position is not identity authority. A small read-only extension of the existing session map/introspection may expose the bound observation tuples and their existing numeric command addresses, letting the SDK use today's observe workflow without guessing positions. Keep metadata and runtime availability distinct; no second DSP-ID table.

Associate reads/maps with their actual owning host instance and existing lifetime. Headless reload, including a failed reload, invalidates a previously captured map/read authority; browser disposal/failure/recreation rejects or discards pending old-host results. Never rebind an old tuple by position. No globally unique clock ID, applied-state revision or `PlanEpoch` is claimed by this child; full common identity/envelope and structural publication semantics remain the parent follow-up. Use the minimum current-owner/lifecycle check, not two new identity systems.

## Implementation boundary and source reuse

- `crates/effect-compiler/src/prepare.rs::EffectObservationHandle` and `crates/engine/src/realtime/observe.rs::ObservationReader::read` are the data authorities. Native hosts can already access readers. Add at most a small borrowed/caller-output helper if needed for the web facade; do not redesign these types or the observation lane.
- `hosts/host-web/src/lib.rs::ReadyOwnership` owns `effect_observations`, `observation_armed`, the stable typed `session`, effect-slot mapping and `poll_meters`. Add a bounded safe selected-read method and minimal map introspection. Read only selected cells. Keep `poll_meters`, `observed_decibels`, peak/GR aggregate semantics and render arithmetic unchanged.
- `hosts/host-web/src/ffi.rs`: use the current bounded live-host staging/pointer/length conventions, an additive selected-read export and a small result record generated from Rust. Reuse existing command/control staging where possible; if a distinct output buffer is necessary, size/cap it from existing prepared/request limits and account for its bytes. No independent GR transport subsystem, general protocol or whole-session serialization. Existing structs/layouts remain intact; new internal names are unversioned and boundary symbols/tags additive V1.
- `hosts/host-web/web/miso-engine-v1-audio-worklet{,-host}.js` and declarations: extend the existing bounded request/reply path for selected reads and, if needed, read-only map fields. The Worklet message handler only validates/copies already computed resident windows. `process()` needs no new work/message site. One bounded selected batch per outstanding read, with typed backpressure using existing pending-request ownership; no unsolicited stream or backlog.
- `sdk/src/core/boundary.ts`, `sdk/src/headless/engine.ts`, `sdk/src/browser/{engine,console}.ts`, public barrels and shipped-host mirror: expose the same selection/result semantics and actual stable mapping. A small shared `observation.ts` for types/decoding is allowed; avoid a generic analysis framework. Use #775's established generated-layout and error conventions; leave its response Worker/preview DSP path unchanged.
- `tools/parameter-metadata/src/abi_layout.rs`, existing generation/scripts/strict validators and SDK assets: generate only the additive ABI/types actually used. Reuse `CATALOG.effects[].observations`; do not create another capability source. Existing SDK and three-browser harnesses own endpoint tests.

Limits: use existing configured compile/observation capacities and the bounded command/read batch ceiling (a message-count ceiling is not a track-count ceiling). Checked arithmetic covers request/result bytes. No read allocation/loop over all tracks on render, no new render lock/wake, no retained result history, and no capacity proportional to session duration. Off-render result ownership/copying is allowed and accounted for without a new per-allocation taxonomy.

A selected read is **non-consuming**. Do not call `acknowledge` on these readers or borrow the legacy meter reader's `consumed_sequence` as this caller's loss counter. Existing meter polling may acknowledge the shared cell; the new read must neither steal another consumer's data nor conceal loss using that acknowledgement. Preserve sequence numbers exactly so consumers can identify gaps; do not invent per-consumer dropped counts. Full per-consumer accounting belongs to the later shared stream service. The raw latest-value publication already conflates by design.

Validate the complete selection batch and output capacity before returning any success. Unsupported/malformed selections fail the whole read; normal per-item pending/unarmed statuses are successful observations of availability, not partial arming. The read never admits/submits an observe command, so there is no new ack-before-drop path. Duplicate selections may be rejected explicitly for a simpler bounded contract.

## Few discriminating gates, then coherent delivery

1. **Native exactness/selection:** two different armed effect taps on one track, asymmetric L/R and different window lengths. Compare each returned value/span/sequence/blocks bit-for-bit with its existing `ObservationReader`; show aggregation remains unchanged. Include zero/pending/unarmed, unsupported/unprepared/missing stable tuple, rearm old-window handling and atomic invalid multi-selection. Verify unrelated readers/consumed counters unchanged.
2. **Bounds/identity:** batch/byte capacity refusal; no query-owned growth across repeated reads; current-owner invalidation on same-position reordered/replaced session and failed reload; output values remain stable. One existing test seam exercises samples/sequences above 2^53. Do not invent a global-clock test for a claim this child does not make.
3. **Real SDK:** existing artifact evals arm/render/read the same per-effect cases headlessly and via the actual browser host request in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Check raw descriptor units, original timing and lifecycle; fake ports only supplement message-error/backpressure coverage. Keep #775 preview and legacy meter regressions passing. Existing render allocation/callgraph gates prove the new read does not enter `process()`.

Run focused changed-package/native/SDK/type/generated checks while implementing. After the usable endpoint is coherent, build/qualify one candidate with the established official report, fail-closed discovery checks, resource/package/three-browser gates and required CI. No per-helper artifact loop, new harness, benchmarks or optimization. Reuse valid unchanged evidence; rerun tests proportionate to actual fixes.

Astra medium verifies this frozen contract, actionable bugs and false claims. Fix those; optional improvements, generalized subscriptions, extra capabilities and hardening unrelated to the contract are follow-ups, not review blockers. Luna max implements; root owns checkpoints, delivery/GitHub synchronization and cleanup. Existing one-verdict-per-attempt/five-attempt limit applies.

## Parent remains open

After this child the ledger still requires: actual-graph EQ/filter composition and applied-target snapshots/live updates; common selective subscribe/update/read/close with identical-job sharing, full plan/clock/state/content/publication identities and loss accounting; required engine-tapped spectrum with correct FFT/smoothing/gap/underrun behavior, browser SAB/qualified pooled fallback and native/headless pump; packed remote vectors, bounded joins, integrated examples/docs/resource evidence and the one frozen descriptive comparison. Preserve #775's delivered explicit preview. Parent-authorized later items remain frozen mode, arbitrary effect taps, phase/group delay/nonlinear estimates, optional device-clock mapping and extended research/optimization. This child exposes existing per-effect data and does not falsely complete the generic stream or synchronization milestone.
